cues.zh: 所以我认为关键的自律在于推迟编码，先等等，直到设计大体正确。不用做到百分之百完美，但你得处于全局最优解的山坡上。

cues.en: If the numbers don't add up or if your gut feel is bugging you, like for some reason,
cues.zh: 如果逻辑怎么都说不通，或者直觉隐约觉得哪里不对劲，

cues.en: then just wait.
cues.zh: 那就先等等。

cues.en: Like Sam and Frodo, you want to
cues.zh: 就像山姆和佛罗多一样，

cues.en: wait until you're on the slopes of Mount Doom, until you're stirring up.
cues.zh: 等到你真正走到末日火山的山脚下，蓄势待发。

cues.en: And you want to find the biggest fiery mountain and then solve for that. So don't stop
cues.zh: 你要找到那座最庞大的火山，然后去攻克它。所以不要

cues.en: your design when you're at the local maxima. Find the global maxima, the big fiery mountain, and then go for it.
cues.zh: 刚走到局部最优解就停止设计。找到全局最优解，找到那座最大的火山，然后再全力以赴。

cues.en: So for tiger beetle, we were just lucky with this, right? So I'm sharing our experience.
cues.zh: 在 TigerBeetle 上，我们在这点上很幸运，对吧？所以我来分享一下我们的经验。

cues.en: We were just really lucky because
cues.zh: 我们真的很幸运，因为

cues.en: the design had to wait. We had a three point five month
cues.zh: 设计不得不等待。我们有长达三个半月的

cues.en: period for it to simmer
cues.zh: 沉淀打磨期，

cues.en: from March to July 2020 before coating started.
cues.zh: 从 2020 年 3 月到 7 月，之后才开始写代码。

cues.en: And if it hadn't, many of the key design decisions in Tiger Beetle just wouldn't be there.
cues.zh: 要不是这样，TigerBeetle 的许多关键设计决策根本就不会存在。

cues.en: And for many projects, it's easy to skimp on design,
cues.zh: 在很多项目里，人们很容易在设计上偷工减料，

cues.en: yet the design phase is shorter
cues.zh: 然而设计阶段本来就比

cues.en: than the other phases.
cues.zh: 其他阶段要短。

cues.en: So in the design phase, you can sketch, you can sketch again
cues.zh: 所以在设计阶段，你可以勾画草图，反复推敲，

cues.en: without writing code.
cues.zh: 一行代码都不用写。

cues.en: You can think through the system in your head,
cues.zh: 你可以在脑海中把整个系统想透，

cues.en: talk it through with your team to flush out showstoppers,
cues.zh: 和团队充分讨论来排查致命隐患，

cues.en: and you can get a feel for performance.
cues.zh: 还能对性能有个预估。

cues.en: So this is cheaper than diving into coding,
cues.zh: 这可比一头扎进代码堆便宜多了，

cues.en: only to back yourself into
cues.zh: 免得最后陷入

cues.en: everything. So design, it's so nice. You just redo, redo. It's very cheap.
cues.zh: 处处被动的境地。所以设计真的太棒了。随时推倒重来，成本极低。

cues.en: You can iterate faster in design.
cues.zh: 你在设计阶段能迭代得更快。

cues.en: And each time you iterate,
cues.zh: 而且每一次迭代，

cues.en: the result gets like I don't know, it's like it's exponentially better.
cues.zh: 成果都会……怎么说呢，都会呈指数级提升。

cues.en: So you can spend twice as long on design to let the design simmer. And over the course of, say, like a two year project,
cues.zh: 所以你大可以多花一倍的时间做设计，让方案充分沉淀。在一个比如为期两年的项目里，

cues.en: that extra month is only 4%
cues.zh: 多出来的那一个月仅仅占 4%，

cues.en: when you compare it with
cues.zh: 哪怕对比

cues.en: the coding and testing phases. Yet that 4% is going to give you like a 10x
cues.zh: 编码和测试阶段也是如此。但正是这 4% 的投入，能在这几个阶段带来 10 倍

cues.en: impact on those phases or 20x or 1000x. For Tiger Bitter, it was literally 1000x.
cues.zh: 甚至 20 倍、1000 倍的成效。对 TigerBeetle 来说，真的带来了 1000 倍的收益。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: and this, I think, is true, especially with regard to testing.
cues.zh: 我觉得这一点在测试上体现得尤为明显。

cues.en: And testing, I think this is my opinion, but I think testing is what really dominates
cues.zh: 而测试——这只是我的个人看法——但我觉得测试才是真正主导

cues.en: the development of complex systems most of all. And the reason is that for simple systems, people say, well, testing time is roughly equivalent to the coding time. Takes you five hours, take five hours to test, take one day, two days maybe.
cues.zh: 复杂系统开发的核心。因为对于简单系统，人们常说测试时间基本和编码时间差不多。花 5 个小时写，就花 5 个小时测，花一天写，可能测个一两天。

cues.en: But for complex systems,
cues.zh: 但对于复杂系统而言，

cues.en: testing can take longer,
cues.zh: 测试可能需要更长时间，

cues.en: sometimes decades.
cues.zh: 有时甚至长达几十年。

cues.en: This is just the history of these, you know, Postgres took thirty years, and we're still solving EFSyncGate
cues.zh: 历史一贯如此，你看 Postgres 历经了三十年，而到了 2020 年
我们还在解决 EFSyncGate 的问题。

cues.en: So for example, like a tool like Jepsen
cues.zh: 比如像 Jepsen 这样的工具，

cues.en: is terrific at testing distributed databases.
cues.zh: 在测试分布式数据库方面非常出色。

cues.en: But even with Jepsen, if you want to find a bug that takes a week to manifest, you have to run Gepson for a week.
cues.zh: 但即便用 Jepsen，如果要找一个需要运行一周才会暴露的 bug，你就必须把 Jepsen 跑上一周。

cues.en: And then each time you try to reproduce the bug
cues.zh: 接着每次你想复现这个 bug，

cues.en: or you just want to confirm that it's now fixed, you have, again, run it for a week.
cues.zh: 或者只是想确认它是否已经被修复，你又得再跑上一周。

cues.en: This is just how long it takes, right? This is current... The standard of current testing.
cues.zh: 这就是所需要的时间，对吧？这就是当下……当下测试的标准现状。

cues.en: And this is just assuming that the bug can be reproduced. So luckily, we know Super Mario, so there's something else you can do.
cues.zh: 这还仅仅是假设 bug 是可以复现的。幸运的是我们知道 Super Mario，所以还有别的路子可走。

cues.en: But what if we could use a time machine to speed up time
cues.zh: 但如果我们能用一台“时间机器”来加速时间，

cues.en: and reproduce bugs perfectly every time
cues.zh: 并且每次都能完美复现 bug，

cues.en: to shrink the testing phase to a fraction
cues.zh: 从而将测试阶段大幅缩短，

cues.en: of the coding phase?
cues.zh: 只占编码时间的一小部分呢？

cues.en: Let me give you an example. So if it took two years to build Tiger Beetle,
cues.zh: 举个例子。假设构建 Tiger Beetle 耗时两年，

cues.en: what if we could test it in a year
cues.zh: 如果我们只要一年就能测完，

cues.en: instead of four?
cues.zh: 而不是花四年呢？

cues.en: That would be a silver bullet. Because normally, to test something like Tiger Beetle is ten years.
cues.zh: 那简直就是银弹了。因为通常来说，要充分测试像 Tiger Beetle 这样的系统需要十年。

cues.en: At least five years for the consensus storage engine, I don't know if like five years is on the short side. So let's just say at least ten years. So two years to build, ten years to test.
cues.zh: 共识存储引擎至少要测五年，五年可能都算短的了。所以姑且就算至少十年吧。两年构建，十年测试。

cues.en: What if you can test it in a year? Like that's a 10x advantage.
cues.zh: 如果一年就能搞定测试呢？那就是 10 倍的优势。

cues.en: Silver bullet, right? So we're going to come back to this idea of a time machine to accelerate testing. The big idea so far is just that if we see the whole picture,
cues.zh: 真正的银弹，对吧？稍后我们还会回到“用时间机器加速测试”这个想法上。到目前为止的核心思路就是，只要我们放眼全局，

cues.en: we can go slower in some areas
cues.zh: 就可以在某些环节慢下来，

cues.en: to accelerate others and go faster overall. So it's counterintuitive.
cues.zh: 从而加速其他环节，让整体走得更快。这听起来很反直觉。

cues.en: You go slow to go fast.
cues.zh: 慢下来，才能走得更快。

cues.en: And I want to share a few tricks with you now that we've learned along the way when it comes to design.
cues.zh: 现在我想分享几个我们在设计过程中一路摸索出的门道。

cues.en: And the first is that I think there's more to software
cues.zh: 首先第一点，我认为软件绝不只是

cues.en: than
cues.zh: 简简单单的

cues.en: engineering.
cues.zh: 工程。

cues.en: So if you believe
cues.zh: 如果你也相信

cues.en: that software is at least engineering
cues.zh: 软件至少是一门工程，

cues.en: and also more than engineering,
cues.zh: 但又远不止于工程；

cues.en: that there's a precision
cues.zh: 相信软件既有严谨的精确性，

cues.en: and an art to software,
cues.zh: 又包含着艺术的成分；

cues.en: that there's hard data, cold logic,
cues.zh: 相信它不仅有冰冷的数据、严密的逻辑，

cues.en: and also what people bring to the table,
cues.zh: 还有人赋予其中的价值：

cues.en: human experience,
cues.zh: 人类的经验、

cues.en: creativity,
cues.zh: 创造力、

cues.en: information,
cues.zh: 信息，

cues.en: inspiration.
cues.zh: 以及灵感。

cues.en: You know my favorite coder is Kevin Flynn.
cues.zh: 你们知道，我最喜欢的程序员其实是 Kevin Flynn。

cues.en: And Kevin Flynn saw a perfection to software,
cues.zh: Kevin Flynn 看到了软件的极致完美，

cues.en: what he called
cues.zh: 他称之为

cues.en: bio digital jazz,
cues.zh: “生物数字爵士”（bio digital jazz），

cues.en: which I just love saying in every talk I give, right? And bio digital jazz is like a tight beat. It's like the hard logic, cold
cues.zh: 我每次演讲都特别喜欢提这个词，对吧？生物数字爵士就像紧凑的节拍。就像严密的逻辑、冰冷的

cues.en: data. It's a tight beat, but it's also a rare groove, something organic, something human.
cues.zh: 数据。节奏紧凑，但又带有一种罕见的律动，是有机的、富有人情味的。

cues.en: So if software is an art like this, or if you want it to be,
cues.zh: 如果软件也是这样一种艺术，或者你希望它是，

cues.en: then the first step is to decide what kind of art do you want to make.
cues.zh: 那么第一步就是决定你想创作什么样的艺术。

cues.en: And here, there's a great analogy from
cues.zh: 这里有个非常好的类比，来自

cues.en: Daniel Lenoir,
cues.zh: Daniel Lenoir，

cues.en: the music producer.
cues.zh: 一位音乐制作人。

cues.en: He has the saying that there are two kinds of musicians.
cues.zh: 他常说，音乐家分两种。

cues.en: There are sculptors and there are painters.
cues.zh: 一种是雕塑家，一种是画家。

cues.en: Musicians who sculpt are like Bob Molley,
cues.zh: 雕塑型的音乐家就像 Bob Marley，

cues.en: recording an album. So they start with something existing,
cues.zh: 录制专辑那样。他们从现成的东西开始，

cues.en: a wall of sound,
cues.zh: 比如一整面“声音之墙”，

cues.en: like a big block of marble,
cues.zh: 就像一大块大理石，

cues.en: and then they chip away, chip away, chip away,
cues.zh: 然后一点一点敲打、削减、雕琢，

cues.en: and then they strip it right down to reggae, which is amazing. All the holes in the sound.
cues.zh: 最终洗练成雷鬼乐，太不可思议了。声音里全是留白。

cues.en: But a band like the Beatles are
cues.zh: 但像 The Beatles 这样的乐队则是

cues.en: painters. So they start with nothing.
cues.zh: 画家。他们从零开始。

cues.en: Maybe a bathtub and some chains, right?
cues.zh: 也许就一个浴缸和几根链条，对吧？

cues.en: They start with nothing, a piece of paper,
cues.zh: 他们从无到有，面对一张白纸，

cues.en: and they sketch and they draw. I mean, studied painting, like they studied art, I think Lennon and McCartney at least.
cues.zh: 起草稿、画素描。我是说，他们学过画画，学过艺术，至少 Lennon 和 McCartney 学过。

cues.en: They sketch and they draw.
cues.zh: 他们勾勒轮廓、画草图。

cues.en: And then they splash color, layer on paint to arrive exactly where they mean to be.
cues.zh: 然后泼洒色彩、层层上色，最终精确抵达他们想要的境界。

cues.en: A painter is never lost,
cues.zh: 画家从不迷茫，

cues.en: but arrives exactly where they mean to be. So I love Bob Marley and I love the Beatles.
cues.zh: 总能准确抵达想去的地方。所以我既爱 Bob Marley，也爱 The Beatles。

cues.en: But I think that most software these days is sculpted.
cues.zh: 但我认为现在的绝大多数软件都是“雕塑”出来的。

cues.en: So you take on all these dependencies,
cues.zh: 你引入了所有这些依赖项，

cues.en: like big blocks of marble,
cues.zh: 就像一块块巨大的大理石，

cues.en: then you hack away and shape them to get where you want.
cues.zh: 然后一顿修剪、剔除，勉强整出你想要的形状。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 然而，

cues.en: we didn't build Tiger Beetle like that
cues.zh: 我们做 Tiger Beetle 时并不是这样搞的，

cues.en: because we zoomed out and we saw that
cues.zh: 因为我们退一步纵观全局后发现，

cues.en: the dependencies were going to
cues.zh: 这些依赖项会

cues.en: slow down testing.
cues.zh: 拖慢测试速度。

cues.en: They were going to introduce safety and performance risk.
cues.zh: 它们还会带来安全和性能风险。

cues.en: So we realized it was actually just going to be faster to paint tiger beetle. And the thing is also you can't sculpt something like tiger beetle because it wouldn't be strawberry fields forever.
cues.zh: 所以我们意识到，直接“作画”来写出 Tiger Beetle 反而会更快。而且关键在于，像 Tiger Beetle 这样的东西是雕不出来的，否则它就成不了《Strawberry Fields Forever》这样的神作。

cues.en: So this is also like a personal thing, right?
cues.zh: 所以这在某种程度上也因人而异，对吧？

cues.en: And I've just noticed that
cues.zh: 我发现

cues.en: some coders have it in them to sculpt. They are sculptors.
cues.zh: 有些程序员骨子里就是雕塑家。他们擅长雕塑。

cues.en: So you'll engage with someone, and they'll always come with a sculpting approach. And that's fine. That's just their style.
cues.zh: 你和他们打交道，他们总会拿出雕塑的那套做法。这没问题，那只是他们的风格。

cues.en: Others prefer to paint.
cues.zh: 其他人则更喜欢画画。

cues.en: And as a team, we're painters.
cues.zh: 而作为一个团队，我们是画家。

cues.en: So we've realized this, right?
cues.zh: 我们意识到了这一点，对吧？

cues.en: And that's where we get our velocity from. So now that we're painting systems out of thin air,
cues.zh: 这正是我们高开发速度的来源。既然我们是在从零构绘系统，

cues.en: the next step is to decide on colors. So I want to give you four.
cues.zh: 下一步就是挑选颜色。我想给你们推荐四种。

cues.en: And for systems, I think these are all the colors you need, right? This is it. Like, just remember this, network, disk, memory, CPU. So Jamie was painting for us in terms of disk and memory. If you understand how to paint like that, network is the same, CPU is the same because
cues.zh: 对系统而言，我觉得你需要的颜色全在这里了，对吧？就这些。记住这四个：网络、磁盘、内存、CPU。Jamie 刚才就是在用磁盘和内存作画。如果你懂了怎么用它们作画，网络和 CPU 也是同理，因为

cues.en: the two textures that all these paints share is
cues.zh: 所有这些颜料共通的两种质感就是

cues.en: latency
cues.zh: 延迟

cues.en: and bandwidth.
cues.zh: 和带宽。

cues.en: Yeah. So four colors, two textures. Just remember that this is how you paint.
cues.zh: 对。四种颜色，两种纹理。记住，这就是你作画的方式。

cues.en: And that's it. And then in the design phase, you do back of the envelope calculations. So Jamie did all the work examples for me. Saved me a lot of time on the slides. Thanks, Jamie. And you can work out all these colors,
cues.zh: 就这样。然后在设计阶段，你要做快速估算。Jamie 帮我做完了所有示例。给我做幻灯片省了很多时间。谢谢，Jamie。而且你可以算清所有这些颜色，

cues.en: work out the shape of your system in terms of network,
cues.zh: 从网络角度算出系统的形态，

cues.en: disk, memory, CPU, latency and bandwidth. You can ensure that you don't have latency spikes, right? And you can see that the system is physically possible.
cues.zh: 磁盘、内存、CPU、延迟和带宽。你可以确保不会出现延迟尖峰，对吧？而且你能看出这个系统在物理上是可行的。

cues.en: So you want to try and sketch as many different solutions as you can in the design phase
cues.zh: 所以在设计阶段，你要尽量画出尽可能多的不同方案，

cues.en: because sketches are cheap, rewrites are expensive.
cues.zh: 因为画草图很便宜，重写很昂贵。

cues.en: It's also worth spending some time to find great names for your components,
cues.zh: 也值得花点时间，为你的组件找到好名字，

cues.en: functions and variables.
cues.zh: 函数和变量也一样。

cues.en: If you take a look at our Tigerstar doc in our repo, you'll find we actually give you tips like how to solve the second it's not the first hardest problem, Alana. It's the second hardest problem. But we give a whole lot of tips. And they're there in the docs, so go check it out.
cues.zh: 如果你看看我们仓库里的 Tigerstar 文档，你会发现我们其实给了你一些技巧，比如怎么解决第二难的问题——不是第一难，Alana，是第二难的问题。但我们给了很多技巧。它们都在文档里，去看看。

cues.en: It's even impacting the Zig style guide now. Like people are clamoring, can we have snake gaze, please?
cues.zh: 它现在甚至影响了 Zig 的风格指南。大家都在呼吁：能不能用 snake_case？

cues.en: But the goal overall is just to have your nouns and verbs just right
cues.zh: 但总体目标就是让你的名词和动词恰到好处，

cues.en: because it shows that you understand the system and you have a clear mental model. Remember, Dijkstra, clear mental model, everything just gets so much easier. So as humans, we have a fault model. We make mistakes,
cues.zh: 因为这表明你理解了这个系统，而且有清晰的心智模型。记住 Dijkstra：心智模型清晰，一切都会容易得多。所以作为人类，我们有一种故障模型。我们会犯错，

cues.en: but good names reduce the odds of miscommunication.
cues.zh: 但好的名字能降低沟通失误的概率。

cues.en: And at the same time, machines also have fault models. So it's important to define your mechanical fault models at the outset,
cues.zh: 同时，机器也有故障模型。所以在一开始就定义好你的机器故障模型很重要，

cues.en: network fault model, storage fault model, memory fault model, CPU fault model. For some projects, like Jamie mentioned, like Tiger Beetle, I think it's okay. You just say, look, memory fault model is use ECC memory.
cues.zh: 网络故障模型、存储故障模型、内存故障模型、CPU 故障模型。对某些项目，像 Jamie 提到的 Tiger Beetle，我觉得可以。你只要说：看，内存故障模型就是使用 ECC 内存。

cues.en: And but memory allocation failure must be safely handled. You have to handle it. You can't just panic, right, if you're a database.
cues.zh: 而且内存分配失败必须被安全处理。你必须处理它。如果你在做数据库，就不能直接 panic，对吧。

cues.en: For other projects, at least this is our fault model. For other projects,
cues.zh: 对其它项目来说，至少这是我们的故障模型。对其它项目来说，

cues.en: even ECC memory might not be enough.
cues.zh: 连 ECC 内存可能都不够。

cues.en: And then you're also considering CPU faults, like things at massive scale, and you're looking to Byzantine fault tolerance. But the big point is just be explicit upfront

cues.zh: 那只是

cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: Use a while true loop. Otherwise, you should never be using that.
cues.zh: 要用 while true 循环。除此之外，你绝不应该使用它。

cues.en: Use... It's safer to use a finite for loop with a fixed upper bound.
cues.zh: 用……更安全的做法是使用带固定上界的有限 for 循环。

cues.en: Then you can detect runaway loops that can deadlock production.
cues.zh: 这样你就能检测出可能导致生产环境死锁的失控循环。

cues.en: Otherwise, you're going to have the system in production and you're to try and now figure out why is this thing deadlocked.
cues.zh: 否则，生产系统上线后，你就得试着弄清楚这东西为什么死锁了。

cues.en: It's going to be a while true loop.
cues.zh: 它准是个 while true 循环。

cues.en: If you limit your loops with assertions, you're going to figure that out much quicker.
cues.zh: 如果你用断言限制循环，就能更快查明原因。

cues.en: And again, the upper bound here is only half the story.
cues.zh: 再说一次，这里设置上界只是一半。

cues.en: So think like a hacker, you have to assert the lower bound. So you expect that the loop will run some minimum amount of time. That's the hacker thing to do. So minimum bound, maximum bound, how many times you expect it to be run.
cues.zh: 所以要像黑客一样思考，你还必须断言下界。也就是你预期循环至少会运行多长时间。这才是黑客会做的事。所以要有下界、上界，以及你期望它运行多少次。

cues.zh: 它就是一团软趴趴的东西，

cues.zh: 然后，

cues.zh: 因为要是没有这个断言，

cues.zh: 我认为问题始于语言层面。

cues.en: So again,
cues.zh: 再说一次，

cues.en: I use this quite often,
cues.zh: 我经常引用这句话，

cues.en: but Barbara Liscov said that if you want to teach or you want to communicate new ideas to programmers, you have to give them new programming languages to think in. But sometimes our languages take assertions away from us
cues.zh: Barbara Liskov 说过，如果你想向程序员传授或交流新思想，就必须给他们一套用于思考的新编程语言。但有时我们的语言却剥夺了断言，

cues.en: or they default to switching them off in in safe bolts, right, in production, which is ironic
cues.zh: 或者默认在生产环境的安全模式下把断言关掉，这很讽刺，

cues.en: because that's where bugs have the most power to do damage, in production.
cues.zh: 因为生产环境才是 bug 最能造成破坏的地方。

cues.en: So we switch... This is what we do. We go into production, we switch off all our safety checks.
cues.zh: 于是我们……我们通常的做法是：一上生产环境，就把所有安全检查都关掉。

cues.en: And that doesn't make sense.
cues.zh: 这根本讲不通。

cues.en: For example, like Go is a modern systems language.
cues.zh: 比如，Go 是一门现代系统编程语言。

cues.en: And it's really like Go is a great language
cues.zh: 而且确实，Go 是一门很棒的语言

cues.en: for many reasons.
cues.zh: 原因有很多。

cues.en: And we use Go, like, in the workshop at Tiger Beetle for some of our operations stuff. And we like Go, right? But in the FAQ,
cues.zh: 我们在 Tiger Beetle 的工作坊里也会用 Go，做一些运维相关的东西。我们喜欢 Go，对吧？但在 FAQ 里，

cues.en: we discover that Go does not have assertions.
cues.zh: 我们发现 Go 没有断言。

cues.en: So while they are undeniably convenient,
cues.zh: 所以，尽管断言无疑很方便，

cues.en: Go's experience has been that programmers use them as a crutch to avoid thinking about proper error handling and reporting.
cues.zh: 但 Go 的经验是，程序员会把它们当作拐杖，逃避思考正确的错误处理和报告。

cues.en: So proper error handling means that servers continue to operate instead of crashing after a non fatal error.
cues.zh: 正确的错误处理意味着，服务器在遇到非致命错误后还能继续运行，而不是崩溃。

cues.en: So there's a few problems with this answer, think. It means well.
cues.zh: 所以我觉得这个回答有几个问题。它本意是好的。

cues.zh: 但问题是，就像断言一样，

cues.en: when you truly understand them, it's not about convenience.

cues.zh: 而是正确性，

cues.zh: 当然，有些程序员可能会误用

cues.zh: 断言来做错误处理

cues.en: instead of just doing error handling.
cues.zh: 而不是直接做错误处理。

cues.en: But it doesn't follow that we should therefore be deprived of assertions at a language level.
cues.zh: 但这并不意味着，因此我们就应该在语言层面被剥夺断言。

cues.en: And most of all, the answer conflates
cues.zh: 最重要的是，这个回答混淆了

cues.en: operating errors,
cues.zh: 运行错误，

cues.en: which are errors that you can handle
cues.zh: 也就是你可以处理的错误

cues.en: with programming errors or bugs,
cues.zh: 和编程错误或 bug，

cues.en: which are errors you can't.

cues.zh: 所以内存不足时，你尝试 malloc，拿到错误，就别再接受更多网络连接。不要用全局 panic 崩溃。那样做不好，因为那样任何人都能 DDoS 你，对吧？

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.zh: 而且显然，断言

cues.zh: 不应该用来处理这样的运行错误，因为断言是用来捕获坏代码的。换句话说，正如我们所说，这是编程错误，也就是某个 bug 即将导致意外结果。

cues.en: But you might wonder, if I can detect programming error,
cues.zh: 但你可能会想，如果我能检测到编程错误，

cues.zh: 为什么不能处理它？

cues.zh: 所以我要提前想到所有 bug 并处理它们，对吧？

cues.zh: 答案是，如果你能预测一个 bug 并正确处理它，为什么不一开始就修好它？

cues.en: By definition,
cues.zh: 根据定义，

cues.en: bugs can't be predicted. There is no proper handling. You're into undefined logic territory.
cues.zh: bug 是无法预测的。不存在正确处理。你已经进入未定义逻辑的领域。

cues.en: You can't continue to operate. And then someone will ask, well, how can you put assertions in a database that's meant to be highly available?
cues.zh: 你不能继续运行。然后有人会问，那你怎么能把断言放进一个本应高可用的数据库里？

cues.en: And I think you can because correctness is more important.
cues.zh: 我认为可以，因为正确性更重要。

cues.zh: 关闭是有代价的，但不关闭的代价更大。比如，如果你知道，对吧，

cues.zh: 我不这么认为，对吧？问题不是要不要停机，而是看我们能多快停机？

cues.en: Because if you're going to shut down manually or automatically, that could be the difference between your business staying in business or going out of business.
cues.zh: 因为无论手动还是自动停机，这可能决定你的业务是继续存活还是倒闭。

cues.zh: 所以这里，断言能很好地帮你自动化这件事。一旦碰到有 bug 的代码，就停机

cues.zh: 而且别在生产环境把它关掉
